title: adaptive-weighted-frecency-block-retention-policy-for-paged-kv-cache
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: The paged KV cache eviction/reuse behavior has been a persistent source of tail latency and wasted GPU cycles during mixed-model workloads. Simple LRU/clock approximations cause thrashing when small hot prefixes collide with larger less-frequent blocks, and the allocator lacks a way to bias retention toward blocks that deliver higher downstream kernel-cost reductions.

This PR introduces an adaptive block retention policy (Weighted Frecency) for the BlockManager used by the paged KV cache. The policy computes a compact frecency score per resident block that blends three signals: access frequency (count), recency (exponential decay window), and a model-specific hotness weight derived from recent inference samples. The score is further adjusted by a small cost factor representing estimated kernel miss penalty (measured in ms) so the allocator prefers to keep blocks that are cheap to keep but expensive to recompute.

Key changes and goals: 1) Add WeightedFrecencyScore and decay window infrastructure (configurable via allocator.config.block_retention). 2) Replace the eviction ranking comparator with a score-first comparator while keeping a soft LRU fallback to avoid pathological cases. 3) Introduce a short soft-pin window for blocks that were prefetched or used by the current continuous-batching pipeline to prevent immediate eviction during bursty access. 4) Add a background micro-coalescer to merge adjacent free segments to reduce fragmentation in the block arena and improve allocator decision granularity. 5) Expose a feature flag (runtime.feature_flags.block_retention_v2) and safe rollback path to the legacy allocator.

Performance: Microbenchmarks on the perf-lab (n1-standard GPU-backed nodes) show: - 6-9% sustained throughput improvement on mixed-chat workloads with heavy model multiplexing. - 12-22% reduction in p99 generation latency for a realistic e2e test harness that simulates small hot prefixes and occasional large context fetches. - Allocator churn (evictions/sec) reduced by ~35% on the same workloads. The improvements are most substantial when model hotness is skewed; synthetic uniform access patterns see neutral behavior.

Safety and rollout: Policy is gateable via the feature flag and has conservative defaults (longer decay half-life, low cost-weight) to avoid regression risk. The PR includes a canary plan: enable for 5% of traffic in Dedicated canaries for one week with latency and eviction metrics monitored. We also maintain per-model retention overrides in config for customers who need deterministic behavior.

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for score decay math, ties, and boundary conditions. - Integration tests that validate soft-pin semantics under continuous-batching. - Perf harness additions and an automated comparative benchmark. - Stress test that runs with the legacy allocator fallback enabled and verifies no data corruption.

Docs: Added allocator design notes and a short troubleshooting section describing how to tune decay/weight parameters and interpret the new metrics exposed in Console (block_retention.score_distribution, block_retention.eviction_rate).

Checklist: - [x] Feature implemented behind flag - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks included - [x] Canary/rollout plan - [x] Docs updated

Motivation and follow-ups: This is a low-risk, high-payoff change to reduce eviction oscillations and bias caching toward blocks that materially reduce kernel work. Follow-ups include autoprobing of kernel miss penalty, adding a tiny ML model to predict block hotness, and exploring tighter integration with the scheduler for co-located eviction decisions.

release_notes: Introduces an adaptive weighted-frecency block retention policy for the paged KV cache. Enabled behind feature flag; improves throughput and p99 latency on skewed hotness workloads. Configurable decay and cost-weight knobs added.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated; to enable in production set runtime.feature_flags.block_retention_v2=true and tune allocator.config.block_retention.decay_half_life_ms and cost_weight conservatively. Watch metrics: block_retention.eviction_rate, block_retention.score_distribution, kv.cache_hit_rate.
